    <item>
      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Kongen fullførte maraton på tiden 4.43.01</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».

      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.

      <title>Macklemore: USA-arenaer sa nei til Fri Palestina-turné</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/macklemore_-usa-arenaer-sa-nei-til-fri-palestina-turne-1.18076286</link>
      <description>Det blir foreløpig ikke noe av den planlagte USA-turnéen til rapperen Macklemore til støtte for Palestina. Årsaken er at en rekke arenaer har avvist ham på grunn av koblinga til Palestina, ifølge et Instagram-innlegg fra rapperen selv.
Blant arenaene som har avvist ham, skal være Madison Square Garden i New York City.
– Etter over 20 års turnéliv har jeg aldri opplevd noe som dette, skriver Macklemore.
Rapperen holdt i oktober konserter i London, Paris og Dublin til støtte for Palestina. Konsertene ble holdt i kjølvannet av at han ble droppet som oppvarmingsartist for Ed Sheeran etter å ha uttalt seg om krigen i Gaza fra scena.</description>

      <title>Ruud fikk revansje i Paris – klar for første semifinale siden mai</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ruud-fikk-revansje-i-paris-_-klar-for-forste-semifinale-siden-mai-1.18076278</link>
      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.
Ruud spilte kvartfinale i Paris Masters for andre gang. For Borges, som står med én tittel i karrieren (ATP250), var dette første kvartfinale på Masters- eller Grand Slam-nivå.</description>

   <description>Die deutsche Wirtschaft wächst wieder leicht. Doch Ökonomen warnen: Ohne Reformen, höhere Produktivität und solide Staatsfinanzen drohen Wohlstandsverluste, steigende Schulden und Belastungen für kommende Generationen.</description>

Thousands of people from across Vancouver Island gathered around Victoria’s cenotaph in front of the B.C. Legislature Wednesday morning to commemorate Remembrance Day.

Officials say it was heartwarming to see community members standing shoulder to shoulder along Bellville and Government streets.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“I’m encouraged in a time, as I’ve often spoke, of declining civility that people, as many people, will take the time to come out and show their support and to demonstrate how meaningful this is,” Marianne Alto, Victoria mayor, said.

This year’s ceremony included a marching colour guard, a 21-gun salute and songs of tribute, including an original song called ‘Wear this Poppy Proud’ by local musician and Victoria firefighter Luke Lampard.

Robert Stewart, a Korean War veteran, says all these elements are to help people remember those who fought for Canada’s freedoms.

“Freedom is not free,” Stewart said. “People enjoy their freedom today because of Korean War veterans, Second World War veterans, and First World War veterans.”

Many in the crowd were emotional during the laying of the wreaths, including Anthony and Tracey Maguire.

“I tend to think, oh, maybe it will be better this year, but we both end up in tears over it, and we both just love it, the people, the support,” Anthony said.

Anthony’s father served in the Second World War and the Korean War, and Tracey’s grandfather served in the First World War.

Both say it’s important to support the veterans and share their families’ stories from the war with future generations.

“It’s really good for them to understand the past so we don’t repeat it,” Tracey said.

Others in the crowd were emotional, remembering the comrades they fought beside.

“Today I remember an awful lot of my friends, family members who are no longer here, and it’s just a day of memory for them,” Stewart said.

This year’s Remembrance Day ceremonies resonated deeply with many Canadians.

In Victoria, many remembered Vancouver Island animal rescuer Jesse Adams who died while rescuing pets in Ukraine last month.

Many also remembered the four soldiers who were killed on Oct. 17 after a fire at CFB Wainwright overtook troops during a training exercise.

“Very, very sadly, that’s an example of how risky these lives are,” Alto said.

“Perhaps it just reminds people on a closer-to-home level that these folks choose to defend us, and even in preparation for that they put their lives at risk for us, and this is one moment in time where we can say thank you.”

Residents, staff and motorists are being urged to exercise extreme caution and avoid travelling unless necessary.

Drivers who must use the road are advised to slow down, watch for debris and washouts, and be prepared for rapidly changing road conditions. Motorists are also warned not to attempt to drive through flooded sections of the roadway.

A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery.

Video shows Hegseth taking photos on the empty steps in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh.

As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be heard, and the soldier guarding the tomb shouted that “all visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.”

Sean Parnell, the Pentagon’s top spokesman, said that “while commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.”

“The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored — and will always honor — the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe,” he added.

The tomb is considered one of the most solemn and revered war memorials in the U.S. and it houses the final resting place of unidentified soldiers from World War I, World War II, and the Korean War. It has been guarded around the clock — rain or shine — by a soldier from the U.S. Army’s 3rd Infantry Regiment, also known as “The Old Guard,” since 1948.

Hegseth and his staff were at the tomb as part of a larger ceremony commemorating Veterans Day that was also attended by President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance.

The incident comes less than a day after Hegseth narrowly survived an effort to impeach him by lawmakers in Congress on Tuesday afternoon.

The effort was led by Kentucky Republican Rep. Thomas Massie and backed by Democrats. However, while Hegseth’s critics were not successful in Tuesday’s vote, Republicans may have only delayed efforts to impeach the defense secretary. With Democrats set to take control of the House and Senate in January, those efforts are likely to be renewed.

Meanwhile, Hegseth rebuked the effort Tuesday in his first news conference in months, portraying Massie as a rogue lawmaker and arguing he had committed none of the high crimes required in the Constitution for his removal.

A core part of his argument included the assertion that criticisms of him and his handling of the U.S. military were tantamount to an indictment against the nation’s service members and their successes.

As British Columbians adjust to their first fall and winter on permanent daylight time, Island Health is urging drivers, cyclists and pedestrians to take extra precautions during increasingly dark morning commutes.

With more people heading to work, school and appointments before sunrise, health officials warn reduced visibility could increase the risk of collisions, particularly at intersections and crosswalks.

According to Island Health, pedestrian injuries and fatalities are more common during the fall and winter months, when darkness, wet weather and changing travel habits can make it more difficult for drivers to spot people on the road.

In 2025, a total of 5,909 crashes on Vancouver Island resulted in an injury or fatality.

Island Health medical health officer Dr. Melissa Wan says small changes in how people travel during darker winter mornings can make a significant difference.

“We can all take preventative actions to improve visibility, giving others more time to see one another and react safely,” said Wan in a release.

“Whether you’re behind the wheel, on a bike, or on foot, slowing down, staying alert and making yourself visible can help create safer journeys for everyone.”

For drivers, Island Health recommends slowing down in areas with pedestrian traffic, paying extra attention near intersections, bus stops and school zones, and ensuring windshields, mirrors and windows are completely clear before heading out.

Pedestrians and joggers are encouraged to wear reflective materials, particularly around their wrists and ankles, where movement can make them more visible to motorists.

Island Health also reminds pedestrians to remain alert when crossing streets, even when they have the right of way, and to make eye contact with drivers whenever possible.

Cyclists should use a white front light and red rear light during dawn, dusk and other low-light conditions, along with reflective clothing or accessories.

Health officials say taking a few extra precautions to see and be seen can give everyone on the road more time to react and help prevent serious injuries.

Myo, who was raised in Saulteaux First Nation in Saskatchewan, will serve in the role for five years.

Her LinkedIn profile says she is a fluent speaker of Saulteaux, Cree and English and recently worked as the deputy chief of self-government and senior director of policy and research at the Métis Nation-Saskatchewan.

She also led the Saskatchewan Indian Cultural Centre, where she worked to preserve, protect and promote First Nations languages and cultures.

A cabinet decision announcing her appointment says Myo was selected for the role after consultations with Indigenous governments and organizations.

The selection process for a new, permanent commissioner was delayed and St-Aubin’s 90-day term was extended last month.

The term of Ron Ignace, the previous commissioner, ended in July, along with the terms of the office’s directors.

The Canadian Press reported earlier this year an audit is being conducted on the office, which is tasked with helping to preserve at-risk Indigenous languages.

Half a dozen sources, including former employees, told The Canadian Press that over the five years of its existence, the commissioner’s office has failed to move the needle on strengthening Indigenous languages and supporting research.

Instead, they said, the office focused on extensive travel and hosting one big conference in Ottawa that cost $10 million. They also alleged a toxic work environment, bullying and uncompleted projects, and staff quitting in frustration.

The Canadian Press agreed not to name the sources because they feared reprisals.

In a media statement at the time, Ignace said the office has faced challenges but “we succeeded in laying the foundation for an office capable of carrying forward this significant work.”

Canadian Heritage Minister Marc Miller described allegations against the office as serious.

“But part of holding people to account is giving people the benefit of the doubt, and that includes making sure the due process is respected,” he said in June.
